items.title: Reflecting On Beverages, Alcohol, and Tobacco Stocks’ Q2 Earnings: Coca-Cola (NYSE:KO)
items.summary: The end of the earnings season is always a good time to take a step back and see who shined (and who didn’t). Let’s take a look at how beverages, alcohol, and tobacco stocks fared in Q2, starting with Coca-Cola (NYSE:KO).

items.title: US Debt Just Hit $40 Trillion and the 30-Year Yield Is Still Above 5%: Why Buffett’s Berkshire Owns Businesses, Not Bonds
items.summary: Federal debt just crossed a staggering new threshold while Treasury scrambles to prop up the bond market, and the intervention collapsed within 24 hours. Where Berkshire puts its money instead reveals something most retirees holding long bonds have not yet reckoned with.

items.title: Dividend King pays Warren Buffett's Berkshire $848M each year
items.summary: A decades-old streak just cut Warren Buffett’s Berkshire Hathaway another very large check.

items.title: Walmart Just Posted Its Weakest US Sales Growth in Six Years: 2 Dividend Kings Built for a Squeezed Consumer
items.summary: Walmart just flashed a consumer stress signal that income investors cannot afford to ignore, and two Dividend Kings with decades of unbroken payout growth may be the only safe harbor left for retirees watching their portfolio checks.

items.title: Walmart says it is using $2.9 billion in tariff refunds to lower prices
items.summary: The company told CBS News it will direct the refunds toward groceries and general merchandise.

items.title: A Big Risk In Coca-Cola Stock Is What Its Earnings Step-Up Is Made Of
items.summary: The stock has not been priced this richly against its own sales at any point in a decade, and part of the earnings growth that price pays for comes from an exchange-rate swing rather than from the operation.

items.title: Berkshire Hathaway Has 10% of Its $358 Billion Portfolio Invested in 1 AI Hyperscaler Whose Stock Is Up 70% in 1 Year
items.summary: Move aside, Coca-Cola. The Oracle of Omaha now has an insatiable thirst for the AI boom.

items.title: Big Food Stocks Suffer From GLP-1 Indigestion. Find Bargains in PepsiCo and Smucker.
items.summary: The company, known for its jams and peanut butter, is making a killing on Uncrustables, a highly processed, frozen version of the humble PB&J. Annual sales recently topped $1 billion and now account for more than 10% of Smucker’s $8.9 billion in annual revenue.  Investors are eating up Uncrustables, too.  Wall Street expects Smucker’s earnings to rise 10% in 2027.
